# [Spec, Then Build](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/spec-then-build/)

Agree a written spec and reviewed plan before an agent executes.

Source: `docs/src/content/docs/patterns/spec-then-build.md` (sha256 `c46df3826f31c5f2ea5de9777e0106cfc96a8170993af753c47687fac162f8ab`)

- Pattern ([#the-pattern](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/spec-then-build/#the-pattern)):
  - Three phases: **spec**, then **plan review**, then **execute**
  - The spec is a written agreement, not a long phase
  - Execution starts only after the plan survives review
  - Applies [Problem Before Prescription](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/principles/problem-before-prescription/) to agent work
- Use when ([#when-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/spec-then-build/#when-to-use)):
  - Multi-hour or [unattended runs](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/unattended-runs/)
  - Uncertain solution space
  - Work that spans several context windows ([Context Handoff](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/context-handoff/))
- Not when ([#when-not-to-use](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/spec-then-build/#when-not-to-use)):
  - One-line or throwaway changes
  - Solution fully known and the human holds decisive context: prescribe, and say why
  - Pure exploration: step 1 is the exploration
  - The ticket already states problem, constraints, checkable criteria, and scope
- Anti-patterns ([#anti-patterns](https://stablekernel.github.io/SHRINE/patterns/spec-then-build/#anti-patterns)):
  - "Make it work" as the only criterion
  - Spec prescribes the implementation instead of the problem
  - Skipping plan review, then steering by correction in chat
  - Plan written once, or kept only in chat
